cohort: The study included 2536 unselected pregnant women without any known bleeding disorder or antithrombotic therapy, recruited from a tertiary maternity hospital between 2014 and 2016, who completed the HEMSTOP questionnaire before delivery.
finding: Elevated HEMSTOP bleeding scores were associated with an increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage, with women scoring >= 3 being at high risk, though the overall predictive accuracy of the score for PPH was weak.
